title: NZ Gym Etiquette
meta_desc: Learn unwritten rules for NZ gyms, including weight racks, machine hygiene, and personal space, to enhance your workout experience at City Fitness, Les Mills, and more.
intro: Exercising in a gym can be intimidating, especially for beginners. Understanding the unwritten rules of gym etiquette in New Zealand can make your workout experience more enjoyable and respectful to others. Here's a guide on the essential dos and don'ts to follow in NZ gyms.

sections.heading: Rack Your Weights
sections.body: One of the most important aspects of gym etiquette in NZ is racking your weights after use. This not only helps keep the gym floor tidy but also prevents accidents and injuries. Most gyms, including City Fitness and Les Mills, provide designated areas for weight racks, so make sure to return your weights to their proper place after your workout.
list: Always rack your weights after use
Use the correct weight rack for the type of weight you're using
Don't leave your weights on the floor, even if you're taking a short break

sections.heading: Wipe Down Machines
sections.body: Wiping down machines after use is crucial for maintaining hygiene and preventing the spread of germs in the gym. This is especially important in busy gyms like Jetts and Anytime Fitness, where equipment is used frequently. Use the sanitizing wipes or sprays provided by the gym to clean the machines, paying particular attention to high-touch areas like handles and seats.
list: Wipe down machines after every use
Use the sanitizing wipes or sprays provided by the gym
Pay attention to high-touch areas like handles and seats

sections.heading: Headphones and Personal Space
sections.body: Using headphones in the gym is a great way to get in the zone and focus on your workout. However, it's essential to be mindful of your surroundings and respect other gym-goers' personal space. Avoid wearing headphones in areas where you need to be aware of your surroundings, such as when walking through the gym or using equipment that requires attention.
list: Use headphones to focus on your workout
Be mindful of your surroundings and respect other gym-goers' personal space
Avoid wearing headphones in areas where you need to be aware of your surroundings

sections.heading: Peak Hour Tips
sections.body: Peak hours at the gym can be challenging, especially for beginners. To make the most of your workout during peak hours, try to arrive early or late, and be prepared to adapt your routine. Consider working out during off-peak hours or using equipment that is less popular during peak times.
list: Arrive early or late to avoid crowds
Be prepared to adapt your routine
Consider working out during off-peak hours or using less popular equipment

sections.heading: NZ Gym Culture
sections.body: Different gyms in New Zealand have their unique culture and atmosphere. For example, City Fitness is known for its community-focused approach, while Les Mills is famous for its group fitness classes. Understanding the culture of your gym can help you navigate the unwritten rules and make the most of your workout experience.
